blocks.html: One must not look so much to the number and multitude of the witnesses as to the verisimilitude of what they depose a; so that more faith must be given to those who depose probable things than to the others, even though these be in much greater number b.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.19.9 (De probationibus, c. Licet causam, Innocent III); X 2.20.32 (De testibus et attestationibus, c. In nostra [praesentia])
notes.original: c. licet cau ſam. de prob. c⟨alt:c.⟩ & in noſtra de teſtib.
notes.gloss: Witnesses are to be weighed by the probability of their depositions, not counted.

notes.citation: Digest 22.5 (De testibus), l. Ob carmen (D. 22.5.21, Arcadius Charisius), the last paragraph (D. 22.5.21.3)
notes.original: l. ob carnem. P fina. D. de teſtib.
notes.gloss: Non ad multitudinem respici oportet, sed ad sinceram testimoniorum fidem — where witnesses differ, the judge is to regard not their number but the sincere faith of their testimony, and the evidence that most nearly agrees with the truth. The print's carnem is a wrong sort for carmen.
